trajectory_summary: This call runs almost entirely on the customer's improvisation rather than the rep's steering — she is not the account holder, cannot produce a bill, and has to guess at a number from an unrelated property just to give the rep something to write down. The rep completes his verification checklist mechanically but never adapts to the fact that the actual qualified party (Ernest) is unreachable, leaving the call ending on an unconfirmed bill figure and a promised-but-unlikely text follow-up.
outcome_dispute: The v1 tag is unknown, but this should not be read as a clean booked/tentative appointment: no day or time was ever offered or discussed, and the bill data anchoring the whole pitch is secondhand and from a different household. This is best classified as callback/no_appointment — a text was sent for a bill photo with a vague 'I'll call you back whenever' rather than any scheduled next step.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Qualifying through a proxy who lacks the data
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Now that, I have to ask Ernest because he is the one staying in it right now.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The entire back half of the call is spent trying to extract bill and usage data from someone who repeatedly says she doesn't have it and can't reach the person who does; the rep never paused to consider rescheduling the call for when Ernest could join, instead pushing through to a secondhand, unrelated-property number.

key_moments.stewart_read: The rep learns immediately that the person answering is not Ernst, the form-filler, yet proceeds directly into the standard intro and qualifier flow without addressing who she is, whether Ernest is expected to join, or re-anchoring legitimacy for her specifically.

key_moments.quote: Now that, I have to ask Ernest because he is the one staying in it right now.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a co-owner-absent-with-data scenario the schema doesn't explicitly cover — it isn't a spouse-decision protocol (no decision being resisted) and isn't quite adult_child_decision_maker (no title/decision framing, just 'he's the one who lives there and knows the bill'). This is a genuine gap: the schema has no protocol for 'the person who can answer the required verify items isn't on the call.'
